QUOTE: When both are present, `platform.c` drops the runtime setter entirely, so calling it fails to link.
VERDICT: MISS
WHY: The answer says that on the macro path `platform.c` drops the setter and calling it fails to link. It never says the function is not declared in `platform.h`. It says only that the setter is "declared only in this configuration" for the runtime case, which does not state that the function doesn't exist on the macro path.
